messages:

Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: evaluating dedicated for inference / sizing question

Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close to an internal OK to move from hosted to dedicated, but procurement and infra want a tighter sizing validation and a concrete sequencing for the handoff so we can align network, IAM, and budget windows.

Two asks: can you provide (1) a short validation plan we can run against our staging traffic that proves the GPU counts & batching profile, and (2) a go-live sequence that shows a non-disruptive swap with rollback points (we need to map to our change freeze on 2026-09-02).

I’ve attached an initial peak/steady token histogram from our hosted usage for June–July; happy to walk through it.

Best,
Sam
Senior ML Platforms Engineer
VectorLytics

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Sam Grant <sam.grant@vectorlytics.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VectorLytics dedicated handoff: high-level plan + next steps

Sam —

Appreciate the context and the histogram. I’m looping in Monica (solutions) to draft a short validation playbook and Karthik (infra/product) to confirm gating checks and rollback windows.

Quick preview of what we’ll deliver:
- A 3-day validation runbook for your staging cluster (load targets, KV cache priming, batching config).
- A short set of acceptance criteria (throughput, p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens) and automated smoke checks.
- A sequenced swap plan that keeps hosted fallback for 48 hours and an explicit rollback at each step.

Proposed timeline (subject to your internal approvals):
1) 2026-08-24: Validation runbook delivery + staging test kickoff (you run, we monitor)
2) 2026-08-31: Acceptance review + final capacity commit (GPU pool size confirmed)
3) 2026-09-07: Production handoff window (non-business hours) — rollback window 2 hours; fallback to hosted for 48 hours

If those dates conflict with your freeze, we can shift the handoff earlier or later; call out what works. I’ll attach our draft estimate and MAP.

— Markus
Head of Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: vl-scaling-estimate.xlsx (xlsx), mutual-action-plan.docx (docx)
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Validation playbook draft for VectorLytics (v1)

Team —

Draft playbook attached. Key highlights (please review inline):

- Objective: Show that a Dedicated GPU pool of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (4 pods with 2 gpus each) meets VectorLytics’ baseline 99th percentile latency < 220ms and sustained throughput of 3.5k tokens/sec for their steady window, with burst headroom to 7k tokens/sec.
- Staging steps (DAY 0–2):
  * Day 0: Provision dedicated pool in our staging tenant; apply customer quantization profile; mirror prefix cache with 72-hour warmup.
  * Day 1: Run synthetic replay at 60% steady qps; measure token-level p50/p95/p99 and KV-hit ratios.
  * Day 2: Full traffic replay at their peak day for a 1-hour soak and verify autoscale behavior.
- Acceptance gates: p99 <= 220ms OR < 10% regression vs hosted baseline; no OOM; KV cache hit >= 75% after warmup.
- Rollback hooks: if any gate fails, we scale down to next compatible model variant and revert traffic to hosted endpoint.

Open questions for Karthik: networking (static egress IPs needed?), GKE node taints, and whether they require on-prem HSM for keys.

Next: send to Sam with slight edits and the simplified sequencing chart; include the GKE network diagram and the mutual action plan.

Thanks — Monica
Solutions Architect, Customer Success

Attachment: v1-validation-playbook.md (md)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: INTERNAL: Validation playbook draft for VectorLytics (v1)

Quick infra notes —

- Networking: VectorLytics wants predictable egress for firewall rules. We can offer static NAT egress via the dedicated VPC; need their CIDR and any downstream firewall contacts.
- IAM/KMS: they indicated FedRAMP-ish controls but not full HSM. We support customer-managed keys via KMS; if they later request HSM-backed keys we’ll add that as an opt-in.
- Sizing justification: 8 A100-equivalents is conservative based on the token histogram; recommend we run the DAY 2 full peak replay with the exact batching settings we plan to ship. If p99 and throughput pass, we reduce to 6 GPUs for cost parity and keep burst autoscale to 8.

I’ll produce a short checklist for the cutover steps (drain hosted route, flip DNS, monitor + rollback). Laura — can you own the post-cutover acceptance signoff doc?

Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, procurement@vectorlytics.com

Subject: Final: Validation runbook, diagrams, and proposed handoff dates

Sam —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached are the final artifacts: (1) validation runbook (three-day sequence), (2) GKE network diagram showing static egress, and (3) a compact mutual action plan with key dates. Summary of what we propose:

- Validation window: 2026-08-24 to 2026-08-26 — you run the replay in staging; we’ll remotely monitor dashboards and run automated smoke tests.
- Acceptance review: 2026-08-31 — call to review metrics and confirm GPU pool sizing (initial commit: 8 A100-eq; target reduction to 6 if DAY 2 passes).
- Production handoff candidate: 2026-09-07 02:00–04:00 PDT — non-business hours; planned DNS flip with hosted fallback for 48 hours.

Rollback plan (short):
1) If p99 > 220ms for sustained 10 minutes after flip, flip back to hosted within 30 minutes.
2) For OOM or repeated autoscale failures, fail the handoff and re-run DAY 2 with an increased pool.

Next steps for VectorLytics (please confirm by 2026-08-20):
- Confirm the staging replay slot and provide CIDR/firewall contacts.
- Sign the MAP (DocuSign link below).
- Approve the proposed handoff window or propose alternatives before your 09-02 change freeze.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/rl/EXAMPLE12345
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/VL-1314

— Markus
